sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:26

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:26:1
items.html:
And HBD are in the three first joints of NHY of AK, and HGT in the three middle joints, etc.: You find here four divisions: Keter; Hochma, Bina, Daat; Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet; Netzah, Hod, Yesod. And in order to understand this we must first know the two changes that there are here in relation to the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] Galgalta, AB, and SAG, which precede the Partzuf of Nekudim. The first is the matter of the vessel of Daat, which until now was not among the ten Sefirot, and from where it came out here among the ten Sefirot of Nekudim. And the second is the matter of the Guf [body] of the Partzuf of Nekudim, for until now the ARI explains, regarding the Gufim of the three preceding Partzufim, that they begin from the Keter, as above in Part 5, in Mati [reaching] and Lo Mati [not reaching]; and here he says that the Guf begins from the vessel of Daat and not from Keter, and he counts only seven lower Sefirot for the whole Guf, and not ten Sefirot — that is, only Daat, HGT, and NHYM, as is brought below in the words of the ARI.
And the matter is that you know that the GAR [first three] of the Nekudim are the discernment of the AHP of Israel Saba and Tevuna, which is the first Rosh [head] of Nekudim. Because of the bottom Hey that rose to the Einayim, and the place of the coupling was raised to the Nikvey Einayim, the AHP of this Rosh became, for this reason, the discernment of a vessel of reception and a Guf, and this Guf of AHP is the GAR of the Nekudim, as above at length. So that the two vessels, Keter and Hochma of the Rosh, remained in YESHSUT as the discernment of the first Rosh, while the three vessels, Bina, ZA, and Malchut, came into the GAR of Nekudim and became the second Rosh, which is the Rosh of the Nekudim, as above.
And you already know that all the quantity that there is in the Rosh passes over and clothes in the Guf as well. It follows that since there is nothing in the Rosh of Nekudim but the three vessels, Bina, ZA, and Malchut, there is likewise nothing in the Guf beyond those three vessels, for everything that is in the Guf must be received from the Rosh. Thus there is nothing in the Guf of the Nekudim beyond the seven lower Sefirot, which are Bina and the five vessels of ZA — for Netzah and Hod are here one vessel, as written below — and the vessel of Malchut is the seventh. However, in the three preceding Partzufim, Galgalta, AB, and SAG, that is, before the ten Sefirot of the Rosh were divided into two degrees, and there were complete ten Sefirot in the Rosh, all this quantity passed over to the Guf as well, and therefore in their Gufim too there were ten Sefirot, from Keter to Malchut.
It was also explained above, page 330, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “Now it is understood,” (35) the matter of the renewal of the Sefira of Daat among the ten Sefirot, which is from the discernment of the exchange of the lights. For in the Partzuf AB the light of Hochma clothed in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, and the light of Hesed in the vessel of Bina, and so forth. And behold, this light of Hesed, which is clothed in the vessel of Bina, became the Sefira of Daat, which is the secret of the MAN [female waters] of Bina, as written there at length. For the matter of the clothing of the light of Hesed, which is the level of ZA, in the vessel of Bina, is regarded as Bina having descended to the degree of ZA, as is brought in the words of the ARI above, page 302, item 12, with the coupling of the level of Hochma, where, because of the exchange of the lights mentioned above, a descent was made in all the degrees, so that Keter descended to the degree of Hochma, and Hochma to the degree of Bina. Study it there well.
And behold it has been explained that because of the clothing of the light of ZA in the vessel of Bina, the name of Bina was changed to the discernment of the Sefira of Daat. And accordingly you will understand the matter of the emergence of the light of ZA from the internality of AK outwards, which the ARI states below. For you will find that in the inner Partzuf, called Galgalta of AK, the light of ZA was in the vessel of ZA, as it ought to be. However, in the Partzuf AB of AK the light of ZA rose and clothed in the vessel of Bina; and in the Partzuf SAG of AK the light of ZA rose and clothed in the vessel of Hochma; and in the Partzuf of Nekudim the light of ZA rose to the vessel of Keter. As written above, that a Partzuf which emerged from the light of the Einayim has in it nothing but the level of phase one, which is the level of the female of Keter, which is the essential light; but the level of Bina that is in the male does not expand below the GAR of Nekudim, as above.
And one should not object from this that, since it was explained that the discernment of the Keter of Nekudim is only a vessel of Bina, for the reason that the first Rosh took Keter and Hochma, then the Keter of Nekudim should have been called by the name of the Sefira of Daat, as written, that the light of ZA in the vessel of Bina is called Daat. And the answer is that since it is the discernment of a Rosh, it is called Keter with respect to itself. And further, and this is the main thing, that the Keter has the level of phase two as well, from the discernment of the first coupling; it is only that it is also included, from the second coupling, of the level of phase one, which is the light of ZA. Therefore it is still not reckoned here that the light of ZA came out; rather, only in the world of Atzilut, for there it clothed in the vessel of Keter and is regarded as having come out, as written in its place.
And now you will understand well that the vessel of Bina of the Guf, since it has nothing at all of the light of Bina, for the light of Bina ends and is blocked in the GAR, as above in the words of the ARI, therefore its name is changed to the name “Daat,” since it has nothing at all of the light of Bina. And behold, the reason has been explained why the Sefira of Daat emerged in the world of Nekudim, which is because here the vessel of Bina of the Guf was made entirely empty of her own light. Also explained is the reason why the Guf of the Nekudim has nothing but seven lower Sefirot, which is for the reason that only these three are found in the Rosh as well, which are Bina, ZA, and Malchut.
And here was rooted the division of the NHY into three thirds. And they are according to the three Sefirot mentioned above, Bina, ZA, Malchut, of the Partzuf of Nekudim, which clothes upon Netzah, Hod, and Yesod of AK: the Rosh of the NHY is the discernment of Bina; the Toch of the NHY, which are the middle joints, is the discernment of ZA; and the Sof of the NHY, which are the lower joints, is the discernment of Malchut. And the reason for the division is that in this whole Partzuf, which illuminates in NHY of AK, there are no more than these three Sefirot, for the Keter and Hochma in them remained above the Tabur, in YESHSUT that is above the Parsa, which is reckoned as Akudim and is not counted among the Sefirot of Nekudim.
However, the ARI counts here four divisions, which are: Keter; HBD; HGT; NHY. And this is because there were two times in this Partzuf of Nekudim: Katnut [smallness/infancy] and Gadlut [greatness/adulthood]. For at the beginning of their emanation they emerged in Katnut, since they emerged from the Nikvey Einayim in the level of phase one, which is only the light of ZA, as above. But afterwards the second coupling of AB and SAG was made, as above in the words of the ARI, and then the Mochin and the Gadlut of the Nekudim came out, which are the GAR, as above. The ARI therefore divides them now in the order of the correction of lines, in the manner of ZA that clothes AA of Atzilut, that is: Hochma, Hesed, Netzah in the right line; and Bina, Gevura, Hod in the left line; and Keter, Daat, Tifferet, Yesod in the middle line. But from the beginning of their emanation the seven lower ones emerged only one after the other in a single line, as written below in the words of the ARI. (36) Thus the ARI is speaking of the Gadlut of Nekudim. (N.B. an annotation from the manuscript of our teacher the author: And it is difficult, for there was no correction of lines in VAK [six ends]. Rather, he speaks by way of example, from ZA of Atzilut and NHY of AA.)
And this is what he says, that the Keter of the Nekudot clothes from the Tabur of AK to the end of the Guf, and HBD are in the three first joints of NHY of AK. It follows that the one Rosh, that is, the GAR of the Nekudim, became divided one from the other, for the Keter clothes the Tifferet of AK, while Hochma and Bina clothe the heads of the thighs of AK. And we must understand this. And further, (37) from where does the Sefira of Daat come here, to the Rosh of the Nekudim, seeing that below the ARI counts it among the seven lower Sefirot of ZA? And the matter is that you know that the GAR of Nekudim are the discernment of the AHP that came out of the Rosh, the Keter being the discernment of the Ozen and Bina, while Hochma and Bina are the Hotem and Peh, that is, ZA and Nukva; and ZA, in the discernment of the correction of lines, is the discernment of Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, and the Nukva is NHY, as written in its place.
And it was explained above that through the coupling of AB and SAG, phase four descended from the Nikvey Einayim to the Peh as at first, and then the AHP rose again to the Rosh, and the light of GAR came down to them, as above (page 406, the passage beginning “And the second coupling.” See there. And page 407, the passage beginning “The first light”). And it was explained there that even so no change was made in the previous state, and YESHSUT did not on this account descend once more below the Tabur, but only its illumination alone. See there. Therefore this discernment of GAR is discerned as the discernment of (38) HGT that became HBD, that is to say, that those Hotem and Peh, which were previously in the level of ZA and Malchut, which are ZAT — behold, the Hesed in them, which returned to the discernment of a Rosh, has now become Hochma; and the Gevura in them, which returned to the Rosh, has now become Bina; and the remaining Sefirot, TNHYM, in them have now become Daat. And the discernment of the Ozen, which is the Bina that returned to the Rosh, has now become Keter. And behold, it has been explained how the AHP that were in the GAR of Nekudim became, at the time of Gadlut, KHBD: the Ozen became Keter; the Hesed and Gevura in the Hotem and Peh became Hochma and Bina; and the TNHYM in the Hotem and Peh became Daat.
And know that from here onwards, in Atzilut, two discernments of HGT NHY came to be in every Partzuf. And it is because of the AHP that came out of the Rosh and became a Guf, which are the level of ZA, as above. And afterwards there are the true HGT NHY, which were never in the discernment of a Rosh. And these two discernments are divided at the Tabur of every Partzuf. For the HGT NHY that are the AHP which became a Guf, their place is above the Tabur, and they are discerned as the discernment of AVI of that Partzuf; and the true HGT NHY are discerned as the ZON of that Partzuf, and their place is below the Tabur. And in the HGT NHY that are below the Tabur too, which are the true ZON, there is in them themselves the very same discernment, (39) at the time when they expand into a Partzuf of their own, in that their HGT end at the Tabur and are discerned as the discernment of the AHP that came outside the Rosh of that Partzuf, that is, the true ZA; while their NHY, which are below the Tabur, are the discernment of their true HGT NHY, that is, those that were never in the discernment of its Rosh.
And with what has been explained, the order of the clothing of the Partzuf of Nekudim upon NHY of AK, which the ARI explains here, is well understood. And it has already been explained that in SAG of AK, in which was the beginning of the raising of MAN to the Nikvey Einayim, which caused the emergence of the AHP from the Rosh, in it itself no change at all was made, and the AHP of the Rosh of SAG did not come out of its Rosh; rather, it is discerned that a special Partzuf of hairs came out there, and in it all this great change was made (as above, page 408, the passage beginning “Looks”). See there. Therefore we do not discern here that there is a discernment of HGT NHY above the Tabur of AK, as in the Partzufim that come after it; rather, from its Tabur upwards it is the discernment of the Akudim, whose ten Sefirot begin from the Keter, as above. And that whole new Partzuf, in which the AHP became HGT, is discerned with respect to it only like the HGT NHY that are below the Tabur of the Partzufim lower than it, as above.
Therefore its clothing resembles the ZON of Atzilut, which clothe below the Tabur of AA of Atzilut. And therefore the Keter of Nekudim, which from the beginning of its emanation is the discernment of the Ozen, which is Bina, is found to clothe the lower third of the Tifferet, since the Sefira of Tifferet is the discernment of Bina of the five ends with respect to its vessel, as above, page 330, the passage beginning “Now it is understood.” And it clothes only below the Tabur of the Tifferet of AK, and not above its Tabur, for there it is the discernment of Akudim, and the Keter of the Nekudim has no hold in the discernment of the Akudim.
“And HBD in the three first joints of NHY of AK.” For it was explained in the Inner Light (page 332, the passage beginning “Now we will understand,” and on page 333, the passage beginning “And now we have found”) that the Sefira of Netzah is the discernment of ZA of the five ends with respect to the vessel, and the Sefira of Hod is the discernment of the Malchut of the five ends. See there. Therefore the Hotem and Peh in the GAR of Nekudim, which are ZA and Malchut that returned to the Rosh and became Hochma and Bina, clothe upon the upper thirds of Netzah and Hod of AK, which are the discernment of the Rosh of ZA and Malchut, the Rosh of ZA in Netzah and the Rosh of Malchut in Hod. However, now (40) these ZA and Malchut have become Hochma and Bina proper, for they returned to the Rosh as they were at first. Thus Hochma and Bina of Nekudim have an equal relation to the upper joints of Netzah and Hod, being from the beginning of their emanation the discernment of ZA and Malchut like them. And understand this.
And the Daat of Nekudim clothes the upper joint of the Yesod of AK, which is hidden between the heads of the thighs within the Guf, that is, within the Tifferet, which is the vessel of Bina of the five ends for the reason mentioned above, since the Daat is the discernment of the light of Hesed clothed in the vessel of Bina, as above (page 416, the passage beginning “And behold it has been explained.” Study it there well). And you already know that these Hotem and Peh are included of the seven lower Sefirot, for the Hotem includes HGT NHY, and the Peh is Malchut. You also know that only the Hesed and Gevura in them became Hochma and Bina, while the five Sefirot from Tifferet downwards became the discernment of the Daat, as above. And it is for the reason that the Sefira of Hesed, with respect to the light in it, is the discernment of Hochma of the five ends (as above in the Inner Light, 330, the passage beginning “Now you will understand.” Study it there well). Therefore its force is potent at the time it returns to the discernment of a Rosh, so that it will once more receive the discernment of Hochma. And the Sefira of Gevura is the discernment of Bina of the five ends with respect to her light (as above in the Inner Light, page 330, the passage beginning “Now you will understand”). She therefore returned now to being Bina. And the Sefira of Tifferet is the discernment of the light of ZA in the five ends; therefore, being now clothed in the Tifferet of AK, which is Bina with respect to the vessel, as above, it therefore (41) became the Sefira of Daat, and clothes the upper joint of the Yesod of AK, which is clothed in the internality of the Tifferet of AK. However, with respect to clothing, it clothes only upon the Yesod. And the reason is that the discernment of the vessel of the Yesod is from the discernment of the Malchut of the five ends (as above, page 336, the passage beginning “And now it has been explained”). And it is known that the screen that couples with the upper light is found in the vessel of Malchut; therefore there are three joints in the Yesod, which are the three places of the coupling: Peh, Chazeh, and Yesod, as written in its place. And therefore the discernment of the Daat that is in the Rosh, upon which the coupling is made there, clothes the upper joint of the Yesod, which is the discernment of the Malchut of the Rosh.
“And HGT are in the three middle joints, and NHY in the three lower joints.” For you know that these HGT NHY are the ZAT of Nekudim, which are the discernment of the true ZA, which were never in the discernment of a Rosh. It was also explained that the true ZON too are divided into two discernments at the Tabur: that which is above the Tabur is the discernment of its own AHP that came outside the Rosh, and they are called HGT; and from the Tabur downwards is its ZON, which were never in it in the discernment of a Rosh, and they are called NHY. And according to this relation, the middle joints and the lower joints of the NHY of AK are likewise divided, so that HGT clothe upon the middle joints, and the NHY upon the lower joints.
And there is yet a second reason, and it is more fitting in this place. For you know that the HGT of the five ends are the discernment of the GAR in them, and the discernment of ZA in the five ends begins in Netzah with respect to the vessels, and with respect to the lights it begins in Tifferet, as above (page 331, the passage beginning “And with all that has been explained”). Therefore the Rosh, Toch, and Sof of the NHY of AK are divided thus: the Rosh in them is the discernment of the AHP that returned to the Rosh proper; the Toch in them is the discernment of the GAR of the five ends, that is, HGT; and the Sof in them is the VAK of VAK, which are ZA and Malchut of the five ends, as explained.
And behold, the four divisions in the ten Sefirot of Nekudim have now been explained (see page 322, the passage beginning “And indeed”), which they have at the time of Gadlut. The first is the Keter of Nekudim, which does not enter here into the count of the Partzuf, being the discernment of the male of the Rosh of Nekudim, which is the discernment of Bina and the self of the light of the Ozen, since it has phase two of clothing. The second are Hochma, Bina, and Daat, which from the beginning of their emanation are nothing but the light of ZA of the Rosh, called Hotem and Peh, which came outside the Rosh and became the discernment of ZA of the Guf; only that at the time of Gadlut they returned and became the discernment of a Rosh. And they also have an illumination from the light of the Ozen out of their inclusion with the male, as above. And the third are the HGT of Nekudim, which were never in the discernment of a Rosh, except that with respect to the five ends they are reckoned as KHB. And the fourth are the NHY of the Nekudim, which are the discernment of ZA and Malchut of the five ends.
And one should not object that, since the AHP returned to the Rosh and became one with the Galgalta and Einayim in it, then the Hotem and Peh, which are Hochma and Bina, became one with the Keter, which is the Ozen, and there are here only three discernments. However, you must remember that no further change was made in the upper Sefirot because of the return of AVI to the Rosh. And YESHSUT, which is the discernment of the GE of that Rosh, remained above the Tabur in and of itself as at first; and likewise the Keter of Nekudim, which is phase two, likewise remained by itself as at the start; only that their illumination reached Hochma and Bina at the time they returned to the Rosh, as written further below.
